native_contracts.acceptance: All real-model contracts, bounds and failure semantics pass.

binding_conformance.acceptance: Exact ordered outputs across the same native binary for the C, C++, Rust, Node, Python, Go, Java and .NET consumers (JavaScript objects in ECMAScript property order); each binding's own suite passes; Rust layouts and TS consumer compilation agree with the public ABI/API.

upstream_reference.acceptance: Same-model/backend upstream agreement within declared tolerance; prompt and calibration semantics preserved.

original_reference.acceptance: Results agree with the original Laya implementation's recorded outputs: identical input token counts, probabilities within 0.05 and unchanged decisions except on near ties (the original's top two within 0.05), whose decision may differ; unsupported cases are still refused. A documented per-platform deviation of one answer (docs/COMPATIBILITY.md, Known deviations) has its own cap.

abi.acceptance: Exports, layouts, status constants and installed consumer compatibility match the ABI version in release/compatibility.json.

installed_packages.acceptance: The CI-assembled multi-platform release packages are installed outside the checkout, on this host (the installed release run) and on each CI runner: actual C/C++, Rust, npm/TS/Electron, Python wheel, Java, NuGet and Go packages work and agree exactly; the browser package is checked by the browser gates.

sanitizers.acceptance: Strict ASan/UBSan/leak checks cover real-model and model-free paths (every registered native test, a short stress run, TSan for native and Rust code), and the coverage-guided fuzz campaign meets its budget; concurrency tooling coverage explicitly recorded. The sanitizer, fuzz and upgrade evidence comes from the CI qualify run (native.yml mode=qualify) of the candidate commit or a reused ancestor, or from a host run.

stress.acceptance: A three-hour candidate soak (budgets.candidate_soak_seconds) of the native library, pinned to two physical cores beside the other host gates, that also reaches budgets.candidate_soak_rounds rounds serves the routine stress gate too (at least budgets.routine_stress_seconds). Every round keeps the per-close limits (thread and descriptor or handle counts back to baseline, closed memory within +128 MiB, read after the allocator returns its free memory: glibc's malloc_trim, AddressSanitizer's quarantine purge), with no hangs or corrupted results; late growth stays within 32 MiB from 40 rounds on, and from 1,000 rounds on the soak rule applies to the closed-RSS series after its first quarter (last-quarter median at most 2 MiB above the second quarter's, least-squares slope at most 1 KiB per round). No browser stress or memory soak exists; the browser lifecycle is covered by the browser gates.

linux_matrix.acceptance: Every required userspace/ISA/compiler/runtime combination passes installed-artifact checks; physical CPU evidence is separate.

browser_wasm.acceptance: Real-browser WASM semantics, lifecycle, asset deployment and same-backend upstream agreement pass: every stage on the non-isolated page; on the cross-origin-isolated page the controls, a primitive.json execution byte-identical to the non-isolated page's, and running cancellation.

browser_webgpu.acceptance: Real-hardware WebGPU semantics, device-loss behavior and same-backend upstream agreement pass: every stage on the non-isolated page; on the cross-origin-isolated page the controls and a primitive.json execution byte-identical to the non-isolated page's.

license_inventory.acceptance: Every native, release and browser inventory carries a checksum-covered SBOM whose notice hashes are current, and the tar.gz and zip archives of every platform carry the licence texts (wheel, jar and nupkg contents are not gated); the distributed components' and model's licence obligations are recorded as reviewed in the security review evidence (model_licence).

reproducibility.acceptance: Two independent native builds of one source snapshot under identical pinned inputs install identical library and Node addon files, and contain the candidate library. Browser builds and package determinism are not checked here (package entries are compared across hosts by artifact_integrity).

artifact_integrity.acceptance: Sources, binary/assets and runtime identity match; stale/swapped/modified artifacts rejected; the shipped linux-x64 packages carry the locally validated library and addon and equal this host's package run entry by entry. Provenance attestation of the final artifacts happens after qualification (attest-release).

performance.acceptance: Repeated baselines and candidate measurements meet predeclared per-profile latency, memory, throughput and responsiveness budgets.

security_review.acceptance: A hand-written security review (procedure and evidence schema in docs/RELEASE_CHECKS.md) bound to the candidate source, the runtime pin and its patch hashes, with no release-blocking code issue; check-candidate validates those fields, not the review's content.

upgrade_rollback.acceptance: Runtime/model candidate axes and rollback rehearsed; failed, missing or mismatched evidence cannot qualify a candidate.

cross_profile_drift.acceptance: Identified native/WASM/WebGPU profiles preserve ordered result structures and metadata. Report finite numeric drift and changed decisions on identical model bytes and fixtures; no cross-profile equivalence promise. Each backend must separately pass strict upstream agreement.

native_contracts.acceptance: Every registered model-free and real-model native test passes on the target's CI runner (scripts/validate.py). Fault injection (real-faults, real-c-faults) is registered on Linux only and the QEMU CPU guard on Linux x86-64 only; the report records them as skipped with that reason.

binding_conformance.acceptance: As for tier 1, on the target: exact ordered outputs across all eight consumers of the same native binary; every binding suite passes.

upstream_reference.acceptance: Same-model upstream agreement on the target within the declared tolerance, for the models the target lists (the primary English model).

original_reference.acceptance: As for tier 1, on the target; only the deviations the target lists under known_deviations may exceed 0.05, each within its own cap.

abi.acceptance: The library exports exactly the header's dtl_* functions (ELF dynamic symbols, Mach-O exported symbols or PE export table) and the layouts match ABI 2.

installed_packages.acceptance: The assembled multi-platform release packages install and agree exactly outside the checkout on the target's runner (no scripts/validate.py --packages carrier); where the target lists electron, the released npm package works in Electron as a directory and from ASAR.

artifact_integrity.acceptance: The target's fragment was packaged from the candidate with the validated library and Node addon, and the release packages carry exactly that fragment's native files.

reproducibility.acceptance: Two independent builds of one source snapshot on the target's runner install identical files, and they contain the validated library.

short_stress.acceptance: A stress run of at least budgets.short_stress_seconds and budgets.short_stress_rounds on the validated library, with the tier-1 resource limits (thread and descriptor or handle counts back to baseline, closed memory within +128 MiB, late growth within 32 MiB).

cross_profile_drift.acceptance: Fixture outputs on the target compared with the tier-1 profile's: identical structure and metadata, numeric drift reported, and no changed decision.

notes: This file defines requirements, not successful qualification or a supported-platform claim.
Default browser launch must work; experimental flags are exploratory evidence only.
A report boolean alone does not prove identity, security, provenance or publication readiness.
